text:
jorge: Heads-up — we need a short design call on how routing picks a region for multi-region hosted customers. We're seeing cases where customers on "enterprise" tier get routed to distant region because of a cheaper variant fallback. Can we make latency a stronger factor than variant-cost for premium tiers?

kevin: +1. Current policy ranks by: tier -> variant-compatibility -> cost -> latency. That ordering makes sense for cost-sensitive tiers but sucks for SLA-sensitive ones.

alice: noted the problem in telemetry: several enterprise requests from EU are hitting us in us-east for <model-variant-quant> fallbacks, adding 150-250ms median extra p99.

samira: Is this purely a sort ordering change, or do we need new signals? For example, do we have real-time latency probes per region per model-variant?

kevin: We have rolling latency histos per region/route, but variant-specific tail behavior isn't exposed to routing today. We only have a combined p50/p95 per region for the route.

jorge: Proposal: add a tiered latency threshold that escalates the weight of measured network+compute latency for tiers with SLA. Eg: effective_score = base_score + weight(tier)*latency_ms. weight(enterprise)=0.8, weight(free)=0.1. If variant compatibility requires fallback, we apply a penalty, but the penalty should not dominate for enterprise.

marc: I like that. Two follow-ups: 1) how do we prevent oscillation when latency probes are noisy? 2) how does this interact with quota-buckets and burst policies?

kevin: For oscillation we can smooth using EWMA of latency over 30s windows and add hysteresis: don't switch region unless new region's score is better by delta=12ms equivalent. For quotas: dedicated quota checks happen after region selection; but we probably should check quota headroom prior to routing to avoid selecting a region that will immediately reject.

lena: UX ask — Console needs to show why a request was routed to region X. Right now the trace just says "routed: us-east". We should expose the top 3 signals (tier, latency, variant_penalty) in the per-request trace so SREs and customers can debug rollouts.

jorge: Agreed. Add a compact JSON blob in the trace: {"rank": [{"region":"eu-west","score":642,"latency":42,"variant":"v1-quant"}, ...]}

samira: Also consider model semantics — some variants (quantized) degrade quality for certain prompts. For enterprise customers we may want prefer non-quantized variants even if slightly slower. That ties into Optimize signals (quality regressions).

kevin: Good catch. We can add a variant_quality_penalty when we have eval data per-workload, but default is 0. For enterprise, set a higher default penalty for quantized variants. We should make this configurable per-customer.

infra-bot: deploy-check: route-service-config v2 -> lint OK, unit tests 186 passed, integration gating pending.

marc: For rollout UX I propose an incremental rollout knob: "latency-first" vs "cost-first" preference per-customer. Default: "cost-first" for non-SLA tiers, "latency-first" for SLA tiers. Console toggle + API param.

alice: If we add an API param, ensure SDKs pass it as part of request metadata rather than a separate call. e.g., header: X-Redwood-Routing-Prefs: {"preference":"latency-first"}. Keep it small.

kevin: Draft routing config snippet (working):
```json
{
  "preferences": {
    "priority_order": ["tier","latency_weighted","variant_penalty","cost"],
    "latency_weights": {"enterprise":0.8,"pro":0.5,"free":0.1},
    "oscillation_hysteresis_ms": 12,
    "ewma_window_sec": 30
  }
}
```

samira: How will this affect metrics? Need new telemetry: chosen_region_latency_ms, alternative_best_region, variant_reason_code. Want these hooked into the per-route dashboard so PMs can see impact of a rollout.

lena: Dashboards: add an 'Routing Explainability' panel to route-level console. Show % requests where latency dominated vs variant_penalty dominated. Also surface how many requests hit fallback variant and the per-tier split.

marc: Ops playbook: if a region's p95 jumps > 200ms for >5m, automatically bias routing away for SLA tiers and send alert. Keep non-SLA unaffected.

jorge: Action items: 1) kevin + infra: prototype config and safe rollout with feature-flag for a single route. 2) samira + marc: define default variant_penalty for quantized vs fp variants and per-customer override schema. 3) lena: add console mock for routing explainability. 4) alice: SDK header spec.

kevin: I'll open PR for the routing comparator and include the EWMA/hysteresis logic. Will include unit tests simulating oscillation. Target: dev canary next week behind ff.

infra-bot: job route-service-canary-171999 started by kevin — logs: https://ci/redwood/route-canary/171999

alice: Quick note — ensure quota reservation step is non-blocking for low-latency path: do a fast headroom check (token bucket peek) and fall back to grace queue if uncertain. That prevents a full round-trip on quota failures.

jorge: This is a good plan. If everyone OK I will schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to align on API shapes and telemetry schema.

kevin: OK with me.

samira: OK.

marc: OK.

lena: OK.

alice: ok.
